items.why: After had to, use the base verb.

teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.
solo: Pergunte por que o erro acontece em português e como evitar.
group: Compare erro e forma natural: I had to went home. → I had to go home. | Did you had to wait? → Did you have to wait? | She has to left early. → She had to leave early..
Peça que digam a forma natural em voz alta.
extra90: Cada aluno cria um erro típico seu e o grupo corrige.

facts.label: Obrigação no passado
facts.sub: Use had to + verbo base para obrigação no passado. Pergunta: Did you have to…? Negativa: didn’t have to. A forma had to não muda com a pessoa.

facts.label: Passado de have to
facts.sub: Use had to + verbo base para uma obrigação no passado: She had to leave early. I had to take the bus. A forma é a mesma para todos os sujeitos.

facts.label: Pergunta no passado
facts.sub: Para perguntar, use did + have to: Did you have to call a taxi? Why did she have to leave? Depois de did, use have, não had.

facts.label: Não foi preciso
facts.sub: Didn’t have to diz que não foi necessário: I didn’t have to pay. We didn’t have to stay late. Não é o mesmo que mustn’t.

facts.label: Uso real
facts.sub: Frases úteis: I had to stay late. We had to finish the report. Did you have to work on Saturday? São muito comuns para falar de prazos e viagens.

compare.br: No Brasil, usamos “tive que” e “teve que” com formas diferentes por pessoa.
compare.us: Em inglês, had to não muda: I had to, she had to, they had to. Pergunta: Did you have to…? Negativa: didn’t have to.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Had to is the past of have to.
Did you have to…? is a past question.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Had to is the past of have to. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I had to went.” → Falso (Say I had to go.)
Did you have to…? is a past question. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

“Marco, Sue is not here. She had to leave early this morning.” says Hal. “Really? Why did she have to leave? Is something wrong?” says Marco. “Her son was sick. She had to pick him up from school.” says Hal.
